It is Cobbs' best-known song and features a guitar figure and melody that has appealed to musicians in several genres.  Although it became a regional hit when it was released in Memphis, Tennessee, copyright issues prevented its further promotion and national chart success.  Derived from an earlier song by Bo Diddley, it has inspired many popular adaptations, including "Shimmy Shimmy Walk" by the Megatons and "You Don't Love Me (No, No, No)" by Jamaican singer Dawn Penn.
